transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, I teach, so I know what being tired is, but this isn't the normal teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day tired. 

It's... well, even after I get a really good, full night’s sleep, I still have to force myself to push through everything. Just the normal stuff, like grading papers, making dinner, getting ready for the next morning... it just takes so much effort lately.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?

Yes, I would say so. I mean, most days I can still smile for my students and get through the lessons just fine. But underneath, it feels like there’s this... gray, flat feeling. It just kind of follows me home, and it makes things I usually enjoy, like my garden or my watercolors, seem really far away.
How long have you been feeling this gray, flat mood?

It's been quite a while now. I'd say... about two years and two months. It started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine changed back then, and that seems to be when this feeling really settled in.
Since this began, has there been a period of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

No, not really. I mean, there have been a few days here and there where things felt a little lighter, maybe a weekend where I actually had some energy. But a whole two months? No, it hasn't ever lifted for that long. It's just been pretty constant since it started.
During this time, have you generally felt hopeless about the future?

Yeah, I suppose I do. I don't feel like things are completely falling apart, exactly, but... I just have a really hard time believing I'm going to feel lighter anytime soon. It's hard to imagine getting back to being the person who actually looked forward to going to museums, or starting new projects, or just enjoying quiet afternoons. It just feels like this is how it's going to be.
During this period, have you generally felt badly about yourself or felt like you were a failure?

Yes, I do. I just keep thinking I should be handling everything better. Like with my job... my lesson plans are taking me twice as long to get done right now, and I even had to say no to mentoring a newer teacher. When I do things like that, I just tell myself I’m letting my school down, and I'm letting my family down, too. It's hard not to feel like a failure when you're dropping the ball like that.
